caption: Shells: a ring of light born on each beat, crossing every face of the cube as one ring
why: On a cube, a ring drawn on one face stops at its edge. Shells works in the cube's real space instead: each beat starts a sphere growing from a point on the surface, and wherever the sphere's skin crosses the LEDs they light - so the ring flows over the edges and round the cube as one ring.

It reads where the spheres are from Emitters, which drops one on each trigger and remembers up to eight. Each shell carries a tag (a colour) and an age. Its neighbours: Ripple is rings on a flat picture from a fixed centre; Sprites draws Particles as dots; Shells draws Emitters as growing rings.
steps: **Audio**'s `beat` fires **Emitters**' trigger: on every kick a new emitter is dropped at a random place on the surface (its `random` setting), and lives four seconds.
A **Random hold** on the same beat picks a new random number per kick - the emitter's tag, so each shell gets its own colour.
Emitters' `slots` go into Shells' **slots**, and **Position**'s `pos` into **pos**: each pixel asks how much shell is passing through its place in the cube.
**speed** is 1: a shell grows one cube-width a second. **width** is 0.2: how thick its skin is.
`value` is the **Palette**'s brightness and `tag` its index: rings of light, each its own colour.

try.label: Slow shells
try.text: speed 0.4: each ring takes more than two seconds to cross the cube, so several are on it at once.

try.label: Thick shells
try.text: width 0.6: broad bands of light rather than thin rings - each beat floods the cube.

try.label: Fast and thin
try.text: speed 2.5 and width 0.08: a sharp flash that races over the cube on every kick.
